subject: scorpion
reasoning:
I'm planning the scorpion's proportions and anatomy, aiming for a roughly 0.2m body with a curled tail, oriented facing forward with the prosoma, mesosoma, and other segments arranged along the length.

Now I'm designing the skeleton structure: a root body joint feeding into spine, tail, leg, and pedipalp chains, with separate joints for the chelicerae's fixed and movable fingers, and setting leg height so the body sits around y=0.025.

Working out the spine chain coordinates from the carapace down through the abdomen using catmull-spline points, parented to a root joint, then building the carapace and abdomen as lofted sweeps bound to that spine chain.

For the mesosoma plates I'll likely use simple squashed sphere geometries bound to each spine joint rather than a continuous loft, keeping the poly count low. For color, I'm leaning toward a golden-brown desert scorpion palette with a darker patterned carapace rather than the darker amber option.

Now I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy: a root joint, a three-joint spine chain running front-to-back, a head joint offset forward, and paired jaw joints for the chelicerae, all parented appropriately for the rig.

Setting up the chelicerae with a fixed upper finger on the head bone and a movable lower finger on the jaw bone, plus median and lateral eye spheres positioned on the carapace. Now I'm laying out the pedipalp arm chain with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and claw joints curving forward and outward from the carapace.

Still defining claw geometry...

Pincer joint aims +Z, with rest gap around 0.015 so tips point inward correctly. Now painting the wrist chain with a tapered radius sweep and color, then moving to the walking legs—working out coxa placement under the prosoma and defining carapace/mesosoma dimensions along the z-axis.

Now I'm mapping out the metasoma as seven segmented plates curving back and up, then placing the four leg hips along the body with staggered z-positions. Each leg follows a path from hip to a raised knee joint, down through the tibia, to a foot tip touching the floor, with side-dependent angling for forward and backward-facing legs.

I'll skip the spike detail and keep the tip radius small instead, then add darker color bands along the leg segments to mark joints.

Actually simpler: I'll add small dark spheres at knee joints for visual breaks, skipping the striped paint approach.

For the tail, I'm plotting a curved path of five metasoma segments plus telson, arcing backward then rising and curling forward over the body, keeping total model height around 0.18 with the stinger included.

Defining the tail chain with a catmull-rom spline through those points, then sweeping segmented rings along it with a tapering radius function that creates subtle ripple at segment boundaries to suggest the beaded scorpion tail look, using low-poly octagonal cross-sections for a stylized feel.

I'm alternating stripe colors every other segment for a two-tone banding effect, and capping the tail end with an ellipsoid telson bulb plus a curved spike for the stinger.

Still working out the stinger curve coordinates...

Now I'm thinking through the body shapes—carapace as a scaled sphere, tail radii tapering from base to tip, and which bone joints should parent each mesh part like the carapace attaching near the spine chain.

Placing the median eye mound with paired black eyes, then adding tiny lateral eye clusters at each front corner. I'm shaping the carapace as a sunken half-ellipsoid sitting over the sternum, then laying out the seven tapering mesosoma plates with decreasing width and spacing going back along the body.

I'm also planning alternating banding colors between adjacent plates, keel strips underneath, and a lofted belly mass running from the front to the tail using a few spine stations to give the body a smooth, bendable base before layering the smaller plate spheres on top as surface detail.

Now moving to the head: I'm defining the chelicerae with a fixed upper spike and a movable lower spike hinged at a jaw joint, positioned so they sit between the pedipalp shoulders near the front of the carapace, plus setting up the head joint and preparing to place the eyes.

I'm now laying out the palp chain with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints following a curved path from the body outward, then placing the hand as an ellipsoid at the chain's end and defining its fixed and movable fingers as curved point sequences that bend inward toward the body.

I'll settle on "digit" for the role, and attach the fixed finger bone to the wrist chain's last resolved joint when no tip is given.

For legs and claws I'm setting up distinct colors—leg tan, palp a slightly warmer tan, claws a darker tip color—while the tail uses a dynamic color function compatible with the sweep's string comparison. Now I'm working out the ripple radius function.

Writing ripple radius math...

I'll skip extra decorative touches like dorsal keels, tail spines, or tubercles given the effort tradeoff, and leave out decals too—just considering a subtle mottle on the lower body.
